correctness.rationale: For the specified 4-uniform morphism and binary coding, the 10 observed adjacent state pairs in phi^4(0) form a substitution-closed set, hence exactly exhaust all adjacent state pairs of the infinite fixed point. Every coded factor of length <=18 occurs in one of their ten length-128 phi^3(xy) images, with the reverse inclusion supplied by actual occurrence of every pair. Exact palindrome enumeration over this globally complete cover yields counts [2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,3,0,3,0,2,0,2,0,0], which exclude central lengths 11 and 18 and hence all longer odd/even palindromes. All 28 palindromes first appear by index 195, and the last first-occurrence ends at exactly 196, so the defect formula follows. The included standalone Python code and its complete output reproduce every critical finite comparison; direct recurrence and finite-prefix checks are independent consistency tests, not substitutes for the cover argument.

value.rationale: Palindromic factor complexity and defect are canonical invariants for symbolic sequences. The finding gives a mathematically complete infinite-language classification, not a finite sample: it identifies all 28 palindromes, exact length distribution, longest factors, and the sharp finite prefix beyond which defect grows with slope one. Its unusual bounded-palindrome behavior contrasts sharply with growing ordinary factor complexity and provides a concrete structural invariant for a newly introduced automatic word. Scope is appropriately limited to the specific morphic word.
